title: Continuous no-jump term makes full-space smoothing norm infinite

statement.quantifiers: For the same continuous scalar flag space and EVERY finite t>0.
statement.assertion: For A=(I-H_M)+C_V/k^2, ||exp(-tA)||_(1->infinity)=infinity. The positive zero-horizontal-jump term e^-t V_(t/k^2) preserves arbitrarily concentrated base mass.
assumptions: Non-atomic CP2 base and fiber-constant functions.
Poisson continuous semigroup has positive j=0 term.

outputs: Exact falsifier of an unqualified full-space continuous smoothing bound.
interface.precision: Every finite t; an exponentially small no-jump coefficient is still nonzero.
costs: A bandlimited restriction might give finite bound only with separately charged dimension/cutoff.

proof_mechanism: exp(-tA)=e^-t sum_j t^j H_M^j V_(t/k^2)/j!; positivity retains j=0.
Fiber constant g_B yields ||exp(-tA)g_B||_infinity>=e^-t/dv(B), arbitrarily large.
obstructions: Discrete smoothing with at least one horizontal jump survives.
Does not refute smoothing after an explicit finite band cutoff.

potential_uses.transfer_gate: Check singular no-jump atoms before importing a full L1->infinity bound.

review.source_reported: Internal analytic audits or released-source proof only; exact reported scopes retained in cited source. No scientific suite or formal kernel replay in this extraction.
